effect-first.protocol: Round robin on the five highest-ranked recipe winners at the frozen snapshot. Equal weight per case and opponent. One observation per image order. Positive margin favors the first named method. Check all six ordered pairs from the user's 4,1,3,2 panel and both 2>1 and 3>1 comparisons from the second panel. Record 2 vs 3 separately. Consider promotion only if the candidate improves strict agreement over v2 on these eight comparisons, has no losses vs slider-off controls, and agrees in both presentation orders on a majority of the current individual case comparisons. These exposed panels establish calibration, not independent generalization.
effect-first.state: Image_1 is the original. Image_2 and image_3 are alternative finished edits of it. Choose which edit better delivers the character concept 'Final Boss' as a usable finished illustration.

preference.instructions: Which character would you more readily recognize as the game's final encounter? Look for an imposing, individual design you could recognize again: costume, body, silhouette, or a signature visual motif can carry it. A stern face, generic soldier's armor, or a darker scene alone gives little evidence. A masked figure, monster, or radical transformation can fully succeed. Favor the stronger character effect unless visible drawing damage materially obscures it. Use the middle answer when neither finished edit is meaningfully better.

finished-edit.protocol: Round robin on the five highest-ranked recipe winners at the frozen snapshot. Equal weight per case and opponent. One observation per image order. Positive margin favors the first named method. Check all six ordered pairs from the user's 4,1,3,2 panel and both 2>1 and 3>1 comparisons from the second panel. Record 2 vs 3 separately. Consider promotion only if the candidate improves strict agreement over v2 on these eight comparisons, has no losses vs slider-off controls, and agrees in both presentation orders on a majority of the current individual case comparisons. These exposed panels establish calibration, not independent generalization. This second wording was written after inspecting the first experiment. To qualify as a finalist view it must additionally retain both damage-panel preferences, favor the intact illustration over the two controlled damage variants in both image orders on all three transfer subjects, and preserve a strict majority of the first panel's six preferences. Historical cases are exposed calibration labels.
finished-edit.state: Image_1 is the original. Image_2 and image_3 are alternative finished edits of it. Choose which edit better delivers the character concept 'Final Boss' as a usable finished illustration.

preference.instructions: Which finished edit would you keep for 'Final Boss'? First look at the character: an ordinary person or generic guard falls short, even if impeccably drawn. When both read as formidable final opponents, judge how convincingly each design is drawn. Prefer forms, surfaces, and focal features that read clearly together. Pushing the effect until details fuse, flatten, or become muddy can make a powerful design worse. Give full credit to intentional stylization, nonhuman anatomy, masks, and dramatic light. Choose the middle answer if the finished results are equally successful.

finalists.protocol: Select the six highest-scoring distinct RAW192 recipes at their best measured strength. Compare every pair on all eight cases, both image orders. For each recipe, average the signed preference margin equally over cases and opponents. Zero is a tie. Omission ranks keep the same finalists and strengths.
